subject: community-medicine
title: Vital statistics and health information: registration, SRS, NFHS, ICD and death certificates

steps.tx: **Vital statistics** describe the size, structure and events of a population: birth rate, death rate, sex ratio, age composition, natural growth rate and life expectancy at birth. They are the basis of community health planning. Data come from **civil registration**, the **census** taken every 10 years, and sample surveys such as the **Sample Registration System** and the **National Family Health Survey**. Know which source gives which measure.

steps.tx: Under the **Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969**, which came into force on 1 April 1970, births and deaths must be registered compulsorily. The time limit for registering both birth and death is **21 days** uniformly across India. Heads of hospitals, nursing homes, jails and dharamshalas must report events in their institutions. Some sources quote 14 and 7 days, so rely on the 21-day rule for exams.

steps.tx: The **Sample Registration System (SRS)**, started in the mid-1960s, gives reliable birth and death rates at national and state level. It is a **dual record system**: continuous enumeration by an enumerator, plus an independent half-yearly survey by an investigator-supervisor. Its design is a unistage stratified simple random sample. The **NFHS** is a separate survey run at intervals of several years; NFHS-3 was conducted in 2005-06.

steps.tx: The **ICD** is produced by WHO and revised about once every 10 years. ICD-10 came into effect on 1 January 1993 and has **21 chapters**, with Chapter XXI covering factors influencing health status and contact with health services. ICD-11 was released in 2018 and has 26 chapters. Remember that the ICD is a **classification** of diseases used for coding, not a drug list.

steps.tx: The **WHO international death certificate** has four lines. Line Ia is the disease directly causing death, Line Ib the antecedent cause, Line Ic the **main underlying cause**, and Line II other significant contributing conditions. Line Ic is called the essence of the death certificate and is the key line for mortality coding. Example: renal failure, then diabetic nephropathy, then diabetes mellitus, with hypertension on Line II.

steps.tx: Key rates use the **mid-year population**, estimated on 1 July, as the denominator. The **crude death rate** uses this population. The **stillbirth rate** counts foetal deaths weighing 1000 g or more, equal to about 28 weeks of gestation. Health information is used for planning and quantifying needs, not for measuring people's attitudes, which is a separate purpose of health information.
